changes.historical_text: Each player sends monsters from his/her side of the field to the Graveyard so that he/she only controls 1 Type of monster. As long as this card remains on the field, each player can only have 1 Type of monster on the field.
changes.summary: Two period behaviours with no text correlate. (1) The GOAT variant counts only face-up monsters that actually have a Type (s.faceupfil adds c:GetRace()~=0), both when enforcing the Type lock on Summons and when sweeping the field, so a card on the field as a monster with no Type - upstream names Magical Hats - is ignored; the modern script counts every face-up monster (Card.IsFaceup). (2) The modern script additionally registers an EFFECT_CANNOT_ACTIVATE field effect that blocks activating an effect whose cost changes the activating monster's own battle position when that monster's Type is not the controller's locked Type; the GOAT variant has no such restriction. Chronology unresolved: nothing in the packet dates either difference.

review.notes: Baseline implements lineage v1 (DR1-EN103, Dark Revelation Volume 1, 2005-03-19) exactly. v0 (MFC-048, 2003-10-10) -> v1 -> v4 (HISU-EN059, 2018-11-15) is wording only: v0's 'must send ... 1 Type of face-up monster ... can only Summon or control 1 Type of face-up monster at a time' loses 'face-up' at v1/v2 and regains it at v3 ('Send all other face-up monsters they control'), then Graveyard -> GY at v4; both scripts restrict the count to face-up monsters throughout, so none of it is implementation-relevant. One further diff line is left undocumented as a behaviour claim: the GOAT variant merges both players' groups and issues a single Duel.SendtoGrave(g,REASON_RULE), where the modern script sends each player's group separately with an explicit sending player (PLAYER_NONE,tp / PLAYER_NONE,1-tp); this could matter for simultaneity bookkeeping but the packet gives no period evidence either way, so no claim is made. Remaining diff is idiom (HintTiming | vs +, g:Iter() vs aux.Next(g), brace/newline style).
